main_text.p: & legendum הַיּוֹדְעֵי, ut à Mufarethis notatum : יוֹדְעֵי בִינָה Scientes intelligentiam temporum, 1.Par.al.12.32. id est, Rationis temporum periti. יוֹדְעֵי דַעַת Scientes sensu, Dan.1.4. id est, Praediti scientiâ. Particip. Praeteritum sive Pahul, יְדוּעַ חֲלִי Expertus morbos, Jesa.53. v.3. Infin. irregularis, juxta R.D. Kimchi in libro Rad. לָדַעַת חָכְמָה Scire sapientiam, Prov.24.14. at Ab.Esra facit Imperativum cum ה paragogico praecedente Sagol. Fut. יֵדַע Pernoscit, Pf.138.6. quae forma partim perfecta, partim imperfecta est : quidâ in Hiphil ponunt ; alii in Pihel : at significatio hujus Verbi in istis Conjugationibus loco Pfalmi non convenit. Chald. Praeter. כַּדִּי יְדַע Quùm cognovisset, Dan.6.10. דִּי בַּל־דְּנָה יְדַעַת Quum totum hoc cognoscerès, Dan.5.22. דִּי אֲנָה יְדַעַת Quia ego novi, Dan.4. v.6. Particip. אֲנָא יָדַע Scio ego, Daniel.2.8. Plurali. וְלָא יְדָעִין Neque cognoscunt, Dan.5.23. Conftruct. לְיֹדְעֵי בִינְתָא Scientibus intelligentiam, Daniel.2.21. Particip. praeteritum sive Pehil, יְדִיעַ לְהֹוָא לְמַלְכָּא Notum ad essendum regi, id est, notum fit, Esrae 4. v.12. Imperat. יְדַע מַלְכָּא Scito rex, Daniel.6.15. Futurum, וְאִנְדַע Et cognoscam, Daniel.2.9. תִּנְדַּע Cognosces, Dan.2.30. דִּי יִנְדְּעוּן Ut cognoscant, Dan.4. v.14. quae sunt cum ל loca Dagesch, pro אֶדַע. Niphal נוֹדַע Notum fieri, Agnosci, Cognosci, Innotescere, Notum facere, Animadverti : Praeteritum, לֹא נוֹדַע Neque notum fit, Deut.21.1. Infinit. וַאֲחֵרֵי הוֹדַע Postea quam notum factum est mihi, Jer.31.19. Futurum, יִוָּדַע Notus fiebat, Pfalm.74.5. id est, Infignis, Celebris. Futurum, יִוָּדַע בְּלֵב כְּסִילִים תּוּדַע In animo stultorum innotescit, cognoscendum se exhibet, Proverb.14.33. nempe, quidquid sapientia reconditum est. Paucula quae stulti, & vani scioli norunt, mirè jactant & oftentant, juxta illud vetus : קְרִיא [?]

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points and some Hebrew words in the crowded lines (notably the Imperative and Chaldee forms) are hard to read at this scan resolution; they are transcribed from the visible letters and may contain errors. Where the scan is blurred, the Hebrew carries a [?]. The running head is the Hebrew letter name יוד. The final Hebrew word at the foot (קרי, Qeri) may be a marginal or text marker; I have kept it as the last line of the text. "Pf." and "Jesa" are printed as shown, with long s rendered as s.
